1. Bring up thetadata feature as datasource for backtesting

1. Introduced a automatic holiday + weekends detection feature in thetadata_helper.py

4. Debugged thetadata feature, added summer vs winter timezone adjustment, subtracted 1 min from thetadata
5. thetadata_helper.py Will only consider trading day as start day when acquiring data from thetadata, no further history needed
6. Time sync handling:THetadata works with NewYork time, but polygon works with UTC time. Also ThetaData is 1 min late from polygon data

subject: Order Management Overhaul: advanced order handling of OCO/OTO/Bracket orders did not work in all contexts and brokers. There are also several confusing and deprecated features being utilized and all of these have been modified across all brokers so that the behavior is consistent going forward. Change highlights: - order.type has been replaced with order.order_type to match (most) broker's terminology and to prevent shadowing with Python's built-in 'type'. - order.order_type no longer accepts "oco", "oto", or "bracket". These have been consolidated into the order.order_class parameter for clarity. - order.child_orders is now populated automatically for all advanced order types at order creation time. Previously, each broker object was handling this themselves differently and it led to divergent and inconsistent behavior across brokers (including BackTestingBroker). - stop_limit and trailing_stop are now allowed within OCO/OTO/Bracket children.  Previously these settings were ignored for any non-Simple order class. - Documentation changes to clarify how these options should be used going forward. - Backwards compatibility maintained with numerous checks and warnings are now issued to inform the user if their current methodology needs changing for the future. - Removed BackTestingBroker __get_attribute() silliness. Seriously silly ... seriously.
message:
Order Management Overhaul: advanced order handling of OCO/OTO/Bracket orders did not work in all contexts and brokers. There are also several confusing and deprecated features being utilized and all of these have been modified across all brokers so that the behavior is consistent going forward.
Change highlights:
- order.type has been replaced with order.order_type to match (most) broker's terminology and to prevent shadowing with Python's built-in 'type'.
- order.order_type no longer accepts "oco", "oto", or "bracket". These have been consolidated into the order.order_class parameter for clarity.
- order.child_orders is now populated automatically for all advanced order types at order creation time. Previously, each broker object was handling this themselves differently and it led to divergent and inconsistent behavior across brokers (including BackTestingBroker).
- stop_limit and trailing_stop are now allowed within OCO/OTO/Bracket children.  Previously these settings were ignored for any non-Simple order class.
- Documentation changes to clarify how these options should be used going forward.
- Backwards compatibility maintained with numerous checks and warnings are now issued to inform the user if their current methodology needs changing for the future.
- Removed BackTestingBroker __get_attribute() silliness. Seriously silly ... seriously.

message:
Fix APScheduler infinite loop causing CI timeout

CRITICAL FIX: Added scheduler shutdown in gracefully_exit to prevent infinite error loops

**Problem**: APScheduler was trying to schedule jobs after thread pool shutdown, causing:
- "RuntimeError: cannot schedule new futures after shutdown" repeating infinitely
- CI/CD pipeline timeout after 60+ minutes
- Tests getting stuck in infinite loop on GitHub Actions

**Root Cause**: gracefully_exit() method didn't shut down APScheduler
- Scheduler kept running with cron trigger (every second)
- Thread pool was shut down but scheduler continued trying to submit jobs
- This created an infinite error loop that never terminated

**Solution**:
- Added scheduler.shutdown(wait=False) in gracefully_exit()
- Only shutdown if scheduler exists and is running
- Added error handling to prevent shutdown errors from blocking graceful exit

- test_gracefully_exit_handles_stopped_scheduler: Already stopped case

**Why This Wasn't Caught Locally**:
- Local tests ran in smaller batches that didn't trigger scheduler lifecycle
- CI runs full test suite with coverage, triggering integration tests
- APScheduler lifecycle issues only manifest in complete test runs

- Buy types: buy, buy_to_open, buy_to_cover, buy_to_close

CRITICAL: Move futures accounting from live code to backtesting-only

PROBLEM:
Futures accounting logic was incorrectly placed in files that affect BOTH
live and backtesting modes (strategy_executor.py and _strategy.py). In live
trading, brokers (Tradovate, IB, Project X) maintain ALL cash/position data
internally. Lumibot is only a display layer and must NEVER modify broker data.
Having futures logic in these files could show incorrect account values to
users, creating potential legal liability.

ROOT CAUSE:
Misunderstood architecture - didn't realize live brokers handle ALL accounting
and Lumibot only displays their data. Added backtesting-specific futures logic
to files that process events for both live and backtesting.

FIX APPLIED:

Phase 1 - Surgical Removal (~245 lines removed):
  - strategy_executor.py: Removed ~227 lines
    * Margin requirements dict and function (62 lines)
    * FILLED_ORDER futures cash handling (85 lines)
    * PARTIALLY_FILLED_ORDER futures logic (70 lines)
    * Mark-to-market update method (90 lines)
  - _strategy.py: Removed ~18 lines
    * Futures-specific portfolio calculation

Phase 2 - Move to Backtesting Broker (~170 lines added):
  - backtesting_broker.py: Added margin-based accounting
    * TYPICAL_FUTURES_MARGINS dict (47 lines)
    * get_futures_margin_requirement() function (39 lines)
    * Futures cash handling in _execute_filled_order() (76 lines)

Phase 3 - Portfolio Value with Guard (~20 lines added):

    * Only runs when is_backtesting == True
    * Adds margin back to portfolio (was deducted from cash)
    * Includes unrealized P&L calculation
    * Does NOT affect live trading

IMPACT:

- Backtesting: Futures accounting moved to correct location ✓
- Architecture: Proper separation of concerns ✓

subject: Fix BACKTESTING_QUIET_LOGS to properly control console output
message:
Fix BACKTESTING_QUIET_LOGS to properly control console output

This fixes a bug introduced in commit 57c7c65f (Sept 28, 2025) where
BACKTESTING_QUIET_LOGS=False was being ignored, preventing logs from
appearing during backtests even when explicitly requested.

Root Causes:
1. Console handler was hardcoded to ERROR level during backtesting,
   ignoring the BACKTESTING_QUIET_LOGS environment variable
2. log_message() had an early return based on save_logfile that
   bypassed the logger's quiet logs check

Changes:
- lumibot_logger.py: Make console_level respect BACKTESTING_QUIET_LOGS
  * When BACKTESTING_QUIET_LOGS=true (default): console_level=ERROR
  * When BACKTESTING_QUIET_LOGS=false: console_level respects LUMIBOT_LOG_LEVEL
- strategy.py: Remove save_logfile early return in log_message()
  * Now uses logger.isEnabledFor() which properly respects quiet logs
  * Preserves performance optimization via early return when quiet=true
  * Allows Bot Manager to control logging via environment variables

Impact:
- Bot Manager backtests now show strategy logs when BACKTESTING_QUIET_LOGS=False
- No changes needed to Bot Manager or user strategies
- Performance characteristics unchanged (early return still happens in quiet mode)
- Fixes logging issues affecting AI strategy analysis on Botspot

Fixes issues reported since September 28, 2025 where backtests showed
no logs despite BACKTESTING_QUIET_LOGS=False being set.

disabled, so each progress bar update appears on a new line and doesn't
overwrite strategy log messages.

message:

Problem: Options with good spreads on Monday were being rejected as
"illiquid" (69% spread) because ffill() was propagating Friday's stale

1. Calculates time gaps between consecutive rows

4. Stale weekend data is NOT forward-filled across session boundaries

- thetadata_backtesting_pandas.py: During initial data merge
- data.py: In repair_times_and_fill() which does its own ffill

Fix TradingFee docs: use per_contract_fee for options/futures, not flat_fee

flat_fee charges a fixed amount per ORDER regardless of contract count.
per_contract_fee is multiplied by order quantity, correctly modeling
broker commissions (e.g. IBKR $0.65/contract). A 40-contract spread
at flat_fee=0.65 costs $0.65 total; per_contract_fee=0.65 costs $26.00.

Updated examples.rst, faq.rst, getting_started.rst, and llms.txt.

message:
fix(order): emit identifier and avg_fill_price in to_dict()

to_dict() iterates self.__dict__ and skips underscore-prefixed attributes,
which silently drops fields backed by the `self._foo` + `@property foo`
pattern. Two critical fields were affected:

- `identifier` (stored as `self._identifier`): the canonical order ID.

  can't dedup or look up orders by ID.
- `avg_fill_price` (stored as `self._avg_fill_price`): the weighted fill
  price. The single most important field for P&L and trade review, yet
  never emitted.

This is why the BotSpot order-history MCP tool was returning
`timestamp: null, price: null, order_id: null` for every order —
the listener correctly stored what lumibot sent, but lumibot had
been silently dropping these fields on the way out.

subject: fix: prevent backtesting broker from fabricating fills from future bars
message:
fix: prevent backtesting broker from fabricating fills from future bars

CRITICAL incident fix. The pandas fill path in BacktestingBroker could
silently price every fill at a single bar's OPEN that had nothing to do
with the simulation time. Observed in a BotSpot "Alpha Picks" backtest
where 72 of 84 stocks froze at the OPEN of 2026-04-10 for every fill
across 2022-2024. Root mechanism: when df_original contained rows far
in the future relative to self.datetime, the existing forward filter
caught them and iloc[0]/iloc[-1:] fallback selected the wrong bar.

The fix prefers bars within a narrow future window (2d daily / 2h hourly
/ 5m minute), falls back to the most recent bar at or before the
simulation time, and refuses to fabricate a fill when no bar exists
within a reasonable window of self.datetime. A second-layer
max_fill_distance sanity check (7d daily / 1d intraday) hard-rejects
any fill derived from a bar too far from the simulation clock.

Provider-agnostic: applies to every data source that flows through
PANDAS / InteractiveBrokersREST fill paths (ThetaData, IBKR, Polygon).

to match the branch name (closing the 4.4.60/4.4.61 version-drift),

message:
feat: self.indicators subsystem for O(1) per-bar indicator lookups

New `lumibot/indicators/` package exposing `Indicators`, wired onto every
Strategy as `self.indicators`. The first call for a given
(asset, timestep, indicator, kwargs) runs the indicator over the full
known bar series and memoizes the result; every subsequent call is an
O(1) slice-to-current-bar lookup.

API shape:
  self.indicators.<name>(asset, **kwargs)  # any pandas-ta-classic indicator
  self.indicators.custom(name, fn, asset, **kwargs)  # user-defined

Why: strategies typically recompute indicators over the full lookback
every iteration (O(N * W) across a backtest). Computing once and
indexing the current bar collapses to O(N + W) — the missing speedup
for indicator-heavy backtests.

- `lumibot/indicators/indicators.py`: Indicators class + IndicatorRow
  attribute view for multi-column results
- `lumibot/strategies/_strategy.py`: lazy-instantiates `self.indicators`
  in `_Strategy.__init__` (zero cost if never used)

subject: perf(indicators): O(log N) per-bar lookup + staleness-aware memo + prefetch-aware fallback
message:
perf(indicators): O(log N) per-bar lookup + staleness-aware memo + prefetch-aware fallback

- `_latest_scalar`/`_latest_row`: replace `.loc[:now].iloc[-1]` label-slicing with
  `Index.searchsorted(now, side='right') - 1` + `iloc[pos]`. The old path was
  allocating a fresh slice on every iteration; new path is O(log N) with no
  allocation. Observed on tqqq_median (13-yr daily, 3.4K bars): 54.71s -> 5.59s
  end-to-end. Memoized compute was already one-shot; this fixes the hot-path
  indexing cost that dominated after the compute was cached.
- `_dispatch`: memo key now carries a `(len(df), df.index[-1])` data_tag and
  transparently recomputes when the full-history frame grows. Previously the
  memo was keyed only by (asset, timestep, name, kwargs), so a routed/live
  adapter extending the frame after first call would return stale indicator
  output.
- `_full_history`: try `_data_store` first, then fall back to
  `get_historical_prices(length=_fallback_length)` purely to trigger the
  routed/live prefetch, then re-read the now-populated store. This makes
  `self.indicators` work correctly on routed/IBKR backtests where the store
  is populated lazily. `_fallback_length` reduced from 100_000 to 10_000 so
  the computed `start_datetime` stays inside pandas ns-timestamp range
  (100k daily bars ~= year 1573, below the pandas epoch).
- `_find_in_store`: accepts an optional `timestep`, tries the
  timestep-qualified key first then falls back to the asset-only key. Matches
  `PandasData.find_asset_in_data_store` which keys on (asset, timestep).

feat(strategy): BACKTESTING_START/END env vars override hardcoded backtest dates

Strategies routinely hardcode backtesting_start/backtesting_end in their
`if __name__ == "__main__":` block for local dev. When the same code runs
in a managed container (bot_manager backtest ECS task, BotSpot MCP
start_backtest, etc.) the orchestrator sets BACKTESTING_START /
BACKTESTING_END env vars from the caller's requested date range — but
previously those env vars did nothing. The hardcoded datetimes always won,
so MCP callers had no real control over the backtest window and every run
of a given strategy produced the same ~14-min duration regardless of what
startDate/endDate they sent.

and applies them as overrides before delegating to run_backtest(). New
precedence is env var > passed arg. Accepts `YYYY-MM-DD` or full ISO
datetime. Malformed values are logged and the passed arg is preserved —
no silent fallback to `now` or the epoch, since that would produce
misleading PnL.

Tests: tests/test_strategy_backtest_env_override.py covers both date
formats, empty-string handling (bot_manager sometimes sends ""), parse

subject: fix(strategy): get_last_price daily shortcut was look-ahead biased (Alpha Picks 2026-04-17 incident)
message:
fix(strategy): get_last_price daily shortcut was look-ahead biased (Alpha Picks 2026-04-17 incident)

Root cause
  `Strategy.get_last_price()` contained a routed/IBKR/ThetaData
  "daily-optimization shortcut" that called

      bars = self.get_historical_prices(
          asset, length=2, timestep="day", timeshift=-1, ...
      )
      return float(bars.df["close"].iloc[-1])

  `Data.get_bars(dt, length=2, timestep="day", timeshift=-1)` computes
  `end_row = iter_count + 2` and `start_row = iter_count`, so the slice
  is `[iter_count, iter_count + 1]` — the bar AT sim_time AND the next
  bar after it. `iloc[-1]` then returned the future bar's close.

  In a backtest the full history already exists, so `iter_count + 1`
  could be any bar up to the last row of the frame. When the shared
  IBKR S3 daily cache contained rows extending beyond the requested
  window (observed on 2026-04-17: real-now's daily bar sitting in the
  historical cache), the shortcut returned today's market price for a
  2022 sim-time. Observed Alpha Picks symptom (backtest f2d9ca86,
  window 2022-07-01 → 2022-08-01):

      COP:  get_last_price returned $97.43   real 2022-07-01 close: $90.98
      AMR:  get_last_price returned $136.76  real 2022-07-01 close: $124.87
      NUE:  get_last_price returned $135.80  real 2022-07-01 close: $105.64
      VLO:  get_last_price returned $110.77  real 2022-07-01 close: $107.98

  Actual historical-bars fills happened at the correct 2022 prices —
  only the shortcut was polluted. Position sizing (`shares_value //
  last_price`) ran on the inflated prices and under-invested every
  symbol on day 1, producing a ~2% understated return vs the
  ground-truth run.

Fix
  Change the shortcut to `length=1, timeshift=0` (no explicit timeshift
  means 0). `Data.get_bars(..., length=1, timeshift=0)` returns exactly
  the single bar at `iter_count` — guaranteed to be at or before
  sim_time regardless of what the frame contains past it. No filter, no
  guard — the shortcut now simply doesn't ask for forbidden data.

  No change to `_should_use_daily_last_price` / `_supports_daily_last_price_optimization` gating,
  since those are independent of the slice-math bug.

Why this got past unit tests
  `tests/test_strategy_methods.py::test_get_last_price_prefers_day_bars_for_routed_backtesting_daily_cadence`
  used to mock `get_historical_prices` to return a two-row DataFrame
  `[100.0, 101.0]` and asserted the shortcut returned `101.0` — i.e.
  it was PINNING the look-ahead bug as the correct contract. That
  test is updated in this change to assert the correct sim-time-safe
  behaviour and to whitebox-pin the exact `length=1, timeshift in
  (None, 0)` call signature so a future edit can't silently restore
  `length=2, timeshift=-1`.

Regression coverage
  New `tests/test_get_last_price_sim_time_safety.py` (7 cases):

    * Polluted-frame reproduction — a frame with only 2022-06-30 and
      2026-04-17 rows must return 2022-06-30's close for every 2022
      sim_time. Exact Alpha Picks COP/NUE symptom replayed as a unit.
    * Dense-frame sanity — consecutive daily bars, sim_time mid-day
      must return the last completed bar (not the same-day or next-day
      close).
    * Edge case — sim_time before any bar falls through to the broker
      fallback (no short-circuit on stale/future data).
    * Whitebox on `Data.get_bars` slice math — pins both the safe shape
      (`length=1, timeshift=0` → exactly one pre-sim-time row) AND the
      bug-pattern shape (`length=2, timeshift=-1` → two rows ending one
      bar past sim_time) so a future `get_bars` refactor surfaces
      either regression immediately.
    * Whitebox on the shortcut call signature — fails loudly if
      `length != 1` or `timeshift` is negative.

Operational followup
  The shared IBKR daily stock/index S3 cache has been wiped on both
  `lumibot-cache-dev/dev/cache/v1/ibkr/{stock,index}/{day,minute}/` and
  `lumibot-cache-prod/prod/cache/v1/ibkr/{stock,index}/{day,minute}/`
  (per CLAUDE.md rule: safe to clear, except `ibkr/future/` which is
  costly to rebuild — preserved). Post-wipe counts verified:
  stock/index prefixes 0 objects each, futures/crypto/option prefixes
  unchanged.

subject: docs(investigation): SPX straddle NUMERIC root cause — pct_change fill_method="pad" dropped
message:
docs(investigation): SPX straddle NUMERIC root cause — pct_change fill_method="pad" dropped

The single line that changed in af8df88b and produces the ~2.3% drift:

  - self._stats["return"] = self._stats["portfolio_value"].pct_change()
  + self._stats["return"] = cash_flow_adjusted_returns(pv, external_flow)

Mechanism: `Series.pct_change()` (old call) used pandas' default
`fill_method="pad"`, which forward-fills NaNs in `portfolio_value`
BEFORE computing pct-change. The new `cash_flow_adjusted_returns` does
`previous_values = series.shift(1)` with NO fill — so any NaN in
portfolio_value produces a NaN return for that row, then
`.fillna(0.0)` converts it to a flat 0% return, silently dropping the
real P&L move that accumulated across the gap.

Numeric proof (synthetic series with NaN gaps, external_flow=0):

  OLD pct_change(fill_method="pad")
    period returns: [0, 0.010, 0, 0, 0.00990, 0.00980, 0, 0.01942]
    cumulative:     1.0500  (+5.00%)

  NEW cash_flow_adjusted_returns
    period returns: [0, 0.010, 0, 0,    0,       0.00980, 0, 0      ]
    cumulative:     1.0199  (+2.00%)

Over ~63K minute-iterations of the 351-day SPX straddle, this
compounds to the observed -229 cps / -235 cps / -102 cps drift.

Recommended fix: forward-fill portfolio_value before the call:

  pv_filled = self._stats["portfolio_value"].ffill()
  self._stats["return"] = cash_flow_adjusted_returns(
      pv_filled, external_flow_totals,
  )

This preserves the new cash-events adjustment feature while restoring
the mathematically correct NaN-gap handling (positions are still
marked at the last valid price during an idle minute; NaN just means
"no stats row emitted", not "zero return").

Alternative: rebaseline spx_short_straddle_repro and cite pandas
fill_method="pad" deprecation + af8df88b as the expected-behaviour
change. Not recommended because the ffill semantics are arguably
correct.

The decision is the cash-events owner's — both paths are documented
in the handoff doc.

fix(strategy): forward-fill get_last_price when length=1 slice is empty

When Strategy.get_last_price's daily-cadence shortcut calls
get_historical_prices(length=1, timestep="day") and gets back an empty
frame — observed on 24/7-market midnight iterations where no day bar
exists exactly at sim_time=00:00 — the shortcut used to fall through
to broker.get_last_price, which on the IBKR REST backtest path also
returns None at non-market-hours timestamps. Net result: every strategy
iteration gets None, rebalance_portfolio's `if last_price is None:
continue` skips every order, backtest runs to completion with zero
trades (observed 2026-04-19 on Alpha Picks 24/7 local IBKR: 31
simulated days at Val: $100,000).

Fix: when the length=1 slice comes back honestly empty, retry
get_historical_prices(length=5, timestep="day") and return the close
of the last row with index <= sim_time. This matches Rob's stated
semantics — "if we have no bar at sim_time, the price hasn't changed
since the last known bar" — and mirrors how mark-to-market works
elsewhere in the stack.

NOT a guard. This code path only triggers when length=1 genuinely
returns empty. A bar that's actually returned by the shortcut (even
one that a hypothetical poisoned cache stamped past sim_time) still
goes straight through to the normal return — no rejection logic
layered on. Root-causing any residual post-sim-time leakage from the
IBKR/ThetaData data layer is separate work; it belongs in the data
layer, not here.

Regression test `test_forward_fill_returns_last_prior_bar_when_length1_empty`
in tests/test_get_last_price_sim_time_safety.py covers the 24/7
midnight case: frame has 3 pre-sim-time bars but no bar at exactly
sim_time=00:00; either the forward-fill returns the most recent bar
(124.87) or falls through to broker — never returns None when an
obvious prior-bar close is available.

subject: fix(data): normalize _index_values_ns to nanoseconds when index unit is us
message:
fix(data): normalize _index_values_ns to nanoseconds when index unit is us

Data.get_iter_count() compares a caller-provided `dt_ns = int(dt.timestamp()
* 1e9)` (nanoseconds) against `self._index_values_ns`, which was populated
via `self.df.index.asi8`. asi8 returns integers in the index's NATIVE unit.
Pandas 1.x stored all datetime64 as ns, so this worked. Pandas 2.x defaults
tz-aware indexes to us — so asi8 returns microseconds, 1000x smaller than
the ns dt_ns, and `np.searchsorted(idx, dt_ns, side="right")` always returns
len(idx). iter_count then lands on the last row of the frame for every
sim_time that doesn't exactly hit a bar timestamp.

Observed 2026-04-20 as the Alpha Picks prod $97.43 leak:
  prod BT c4b54459-7be0-4525-877d-9e95275284c0 (lumibot 4.5.1, IBKR)
  COP parquet dtype: datetime64[us, America/New_York]
  sim_time=2022-07-01 10:00 → iter_count=1256 (last row, 2022-07-29 close
  $97.43) instead of iter_count=1236 (2022-06-30, close $89.81).

  get_last_price(COP) returned $97.43 → sized 205 shares (vs ~219 correct)
  → undersized by ~6% → 8.18% total return vs +10% ground truth. Exactly
  the symptom that v4.5.0 slice-math fix and v4.5.1 forward-fill were
  supposed to fix, but both upstream fixes correctly request "bar at
  iter_count" — this bug poisons iter_count itself.

  Local dev cache parquets were written by older pandas as datetime64[ns],
  which happened to work via coincidence-of-units and masked the bug
  entirely. Fresh prod parquets trigger it every time.

Fix: normalize the index to ns via `DatetimeIndex.as_unit("ns")` before
calling asi8. Pandas 2.x supports this; pandas 1.x raises AttributeError
and we no-op (already ns). Either way _index_values_ns now contains
nanoseconds regardless of the source parquet's precision.

Regression coverage in tests/test_data_iter_count_microsecond_index.py:
- test_get_iter_count_handles_any_index_precision[us]
- test_get_bars_length1_returns_sim_time_bar_any_precision[us]
- whitebox pin on the 1000x unit magnitude difference

Full 34-test sweep (new + sim_time_safety + tearsheet + strategy_methods +
data_get_bars) passes.

Verified directly against the prod COP parquet from backtest c4b54459:
  before fix: iter_count(2022-07-01 10:00) = 1256 → 2022-07-29 ($97.43) ❌
  after fix:  iter_count(2022-07-01 10:00) = 1236 → 2022-06-30 ($89.81) ✅
